pattern: crud, kiss, solid, dry, yagni, factory, repository

sprints.goal: Establish core data access layer and database connectivity.

acceptance_criteria.description: Project initialized as a proper Go module.
Database connection package successfully imports and initializes an SQLite connection pool.
Basic database migration utility is implemented to create the initial schema.

tasks.description: Initialize the Go module, establish directory structure (e.g., `internal/repository`, `pkg/model`), and configure necessary dependencies, including the SQLite driver (go-sqlite3) for data persistence.
tasks.title: Setup Project Structure & Dependencies

acceptance_criteria.description: All core entities are defined as Go structs in a centralized `pkg/model` package.
Model struct tags enforce basic constraints (e.g., required, length).
Unit tests validate basic model instantiation and validation failures.

tasks.description: Create domain models (structs) representing the primary entities. Implement data validation hooks on these structs to ensure data integrity at the model level before persistence.
tasks.title: Define Core Data Models

acceptance_criteria.description: A generic `Repository[T]` interface is defined and used for type safety.
Concrete SQL implementations handle prepared statements efficiently.
CRUD operations successfully interact with the SQLite database without logic errors.

tasks.description: Develop the foundational `Repository` interface (e.g., `UserRepository`) defining standard CRUD methods (GetByID, Create, Update, Delete). Implement a concrete SQL repository adhering to this interface.
tasks.title: Implement Repository Pattern Base

sprints.goal: Build the business logic and service layer adhering to SOLID principles.

acceptance_criteria.description: Service layer is decoupled from the database connection details.
Business logic (validation, complex transformations) resides exclusively in service methods.
The Dependency Injection mechanism allows swapping mock repositories for testing.

tasks.description: Define a clean Service interface (e.g., `UserService`) that orchestrates calls between HTTP handlers and the repository. This isolates business rules from persistence logic.
tasks.title: Create Service Interface Layer

acceptance_criteria.description: Critical operations execute within atomic transactions.
Service methods handle application-level errors (e.g., 'User already exists') distinct from SQL errors.
The logic successfully implements necessary business rules (e.g., 'Cannot delete user with active orders').

tasks.description: Develop the concrete service implementation. Focus on complex business workflows that may require multiple database writes (transactions). Adhere to DRY by encapsulating common error handling.
tasks.title: Implement Business Logic and Transactions

acceptance_criteria.description: A dedicated factory function/struct exists for object construction.
The factory ensures that all required dependent models are correctly initialized before creating the final entity.
Code readability improves due to explicit creation steps rather than large constructor functions.

tasks.description: If entity creation is complex (e.g., requiring derived fields or multiple inputs), implement a Factory pattern to construct the domain objects cleanly, adhering to YAGNI principles by only building what is necessary.
tasks.title: Integrate Factory/Builder for Complex Objects

sprints.goal: Build lightweight presentation layer and API endpoints.

acceptance_criteria.description: A stable main entry point serves the application over a defined port.
Handlers correctly parse request bodies and query parameters into Go types.
Middleware (e.g., logging, CORS) is properly integrated into the routing stack.

tasks.description: Initialize the web server (e.g., using net/http or a minimal router). Create dedicated HTTP handler functions that accept requests, validate inputs, and call the Service layer.
tasks.title: Set up Web Framework and Handlers

acceptance_criteria.description: A functional 'read' endpoint displays data rendered from a template.
The update/create functionality uses HTMX to swap partial view sections without page reload.
The UI maintains simplicity and low resource consumption as intended.

tasks.description: Develop the view templates using Go's built-in templating engine. Instead of a full SPA, endpoints should render partial views that are updated via HTMX requests when actions occur, minimizing JavaScript complexity.
tasks.title: Implement Lightweight UI Rendering (Templates/HTMX)

acceptance_criteria.description: A GET /api/v1 route returns a valid JSON array of resources.
POST /api/v1 requires request body validation and returns appropriate HTTP status codes (201, 400, etc.).
The separation between the UI rendering logic and the raw API endpoints is clean.

tasks.description: In addition to the lightweight UI, implement JSON endpoints for programmatic access. These handlers should serialize Service output models into JSON responses.
tasks.title: Develop RESTful API Endpoints (JSON)

sprints.goal: Finalize system robustness, error handling, and testing coverage.

acceptance_criteria.description: 100% coverage on key service methods paths.
Tests demonstrate correct handling of database constraint violations (e.g., unique keys).
Mocking framework successfully intercepts repository calls to prevent real DB interaction.

tasks.description: Write unit tests for the Service layer and Repository layer. Mock external dependencies (database connection) to ensure tests are fast, isolated, and validate business logic edge cases.
tasks.title: Comprehensive Unit Testing Suite

acceptance_criteria.description: The system returns specific status codes (400, 404, 500) corresponding to business/system failures.
Logging captures structured error information (severity, context, ID).
Handlers no longer rely on raw Go errors but use typed application error wrappers.

tasks.description: Refactor global error management. Create custom, typed application errors (e.g., `ErrNotFound`, `ErrInvalidInput`) that are propagated through the service layer and translated into appropriate HTTP responses by handlers.
tasks.title: Implement Centralized Error Handling

acceptance_criteria.description: Database queries are profiled and optimized for efficient bulk retrieval or updates.
The application passes load testing simulating expected concurrent user load without connection pooling exhaustion.
Final code review confirms adherence to DRY principles across all service methods.

tasks.description: Perform a final code review focusing on performance bottlenecks (N+1 query detection, unnecessary database roundtrips). Ensure all resource management (DB connections, file handles) is closed correctly using `defer` statements.
tasks.title: Review and Optimize Performance
